units.function: Mocked HTTP tests for previewing and applying subtree pause/cancel/restore/resume holds, interrupting Runs and queued wakes, changing Issue status, optional Agent wakeup and failure cleanup.
units.dependencyDirection: Supertest/Express -> tree-control routes -> mocked Issue/tree-control/heartbeat/activity services; persistence, graph traversal and transaction semantics are not exercised.
units.keyDataModels: Tenant board/Agent principal; root Issue; hold mode/status/reason/metadata; preview affected totals/warnings/active Runs; updated Issue IDs/saved status; released hold IDs; Run interruption and activity record.
units.lifecycle: Authorize root and optionally preview -> create hold -> for pause/cancel interrupt active Runs and queued wakes, then cancel status for cancel mode -> restore saved states/release cancel holds and optionally wake assignees -> resume releases pause holds -> cleanup restore hold if application fails.
units.testAssessment: Approved unsandboxed run passed all 9 tests; sandboxed run failed solely on TCP EPERM. Coverage checks tenant concealment, Agent denial, malformed IDs, pause/cancel side effects, interruption failure, restore/wake/cleanup and side-effect-free resume. It omits real persistence/graph authorization, preview-to-apply binding, concurrent/overlapping holds, saga atomicity, partial restore, Connector fencing, role/risk policy and per-node responsibility.
units.designRationale: Provide an operator emergency control over an Issue subtree with preview, durable hold semantics, active execution interruption and reversible status restoration.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs organization-wide emergency pause/cancel/restore controls that revoke execution authority across heterogeneous Connectors without losing truthful state, while respecting each Work item's responsible human and approval policy.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT preview/hold/restore concepts, uniform tenant concealment and explicit Run/wake effects. Bind apply to a signed previewSnapshotVersion and policy version; model TreeControlCommand as a durable saga with per-node outcomes, CAS/fencing-token capability revocation and Connector acknowledgements; expose partial/failed interruption rather than reporting clean cancellation; require reason, role/risk policy and approval when appropriate; notify accountable humans and append immutable control receipts.
units.responsibilityConflict: When adapter interruption fails, Issues are still marked cancelled and the API returns 201, creating a dangerous split brain: the control plane says stopped while the Agent may still act. Coarse board access is not accountable authority for every subtree node, and no responsible-human notification or approval is proved.
evidence: git history: five commits from 7f2ed0ad90d7186d108f65400e322bda08dcbfe2 through f98c348e2b3011b2fdc905c7a41f73d4f1998ac3 recorded in the read ledger
2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 9/9 failed on TCP EPERM only
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL split-brain safety flaw for Company OS adoption: failed Run interruption does not prevent cancelled control-plane status or success response. CRITICAL distributed-systems gap: no Connector fencing/capability revocation/acknowledgement or saga proof. HIGH TOCTOU gap: preview is not bound to apply snapshot. HIGH responsibility gap: no role/risk policy, per-node accountable human or approval. HIGH audit leakage: raw adapter error is written to activity. MEDIUM restore gap: partial application compensation is unproven. POSITIVE: Agent denial, uniform tenant 404, explicit holds and restore cleanup are strong starting controls.
